data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel's data shows it allowed half of the promised aid trucks into Gaza
data.author: Elis Gjevori
data.summary:
Israel's data shows it allowed half of the promised aid trucks into Gaza
Israel has failed to meet its commitments under the Gaza ceasefire deal, allowing in only around half the agreed volume of humanitarian and commercial goods each month since March, Israeli military data shows.
Data obtained by Haaretz newspaper showed a growing shortfall in food deliveries to Gaza, alongside severe shortages of medical supplies, tents and materials to repair damaged infrastructure. Torrential rains have flooded displacement camps, leaving hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in increasingly dire conditions.
Under the ceasefire deal, Israel pledged to allow 4,200 vehicles carrying humanitarian and commercial goods into Gaza each week, equivalent to roughly 18,200 a month.
Deliveries were to include food, fuel, medical supplies and equipment, shelter materials and equipment to repair essential infrastructure.
Data supplied by the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (Cogat) to the US-led International Gaza Support Center (IGSC) show that Israel allowed about 4,700 trucks into Gaza in March, rising to 5,300 in April and more than 9,600 in May.

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report
Israel kidnapped two Iranian officials and killed one of them in a decades-long search for an Israeli pilot whose fighter jet crashed in Lebanon while bombing the country in 1986, The New York Times reported on Sunday.
Israeli pilot Ron Arad was bombing Lebanese villages in 1986 when one of his missiles malfunctioned, forcing him to eject from his fighter jet.
Since then, Israel has been on a mission to find out what happened to Arad, leaving a trail of death and destruction in its wake which has left more than 40 people dead and dozens more wounded.
The NYT said that the search for Arad was rooted in the "Jewish tradition" to bring its soldiers back to Israel.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemen hospital faces shutdown risk due to sege on Taiz
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Yemen hospital faces shutdown risk due to sege on Taiz
A hospital in the Yemeni city of Taiz has sounded the alarm over medicine and fuel shortages, warning that it is facing the risk of a shutdown if access to aid and supplies is not restored.
"For two months we have been calling and appealing to the international community, the humanitarian organisations: save Taiz, save health in Taiz, save the Yemeni-Swedish hospital. There is no fuel. We are at our last breath," said the hospital director Sami Al-Sharabi.
The Houthis have besieged Taiz for more than a month as they try to break into territory held by the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.
Since fighting reignited in the summer, nearly 330,000 people have been displaced.
"Save Taiz, save health in Taiz, save the Yemeni-Swedish hospital. There is no fuel. We are at our last breath." data.author: Mera Aladam

China confirms meeting with Trump, Putin
China has confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, are set to hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen.
"On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the foreign ministry said.
The Kremlin and the White House have both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.
According to US officials, Trump wanted to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals as well as discuss the war on Iran.

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Report: Netanyahu's allies open to unity government without Ben Gvir’s party
Associates of Benjamin Netanyahu have told Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot’s team they would accept a unity government without National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's party, according to the daily Israel Hayom.
Netanyahu’s associates said that Likud could let go of Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) if negotiations opened on a broad coalition.
They also told figures in Eisenkot’s bloc that Washington was demanding Otzma Yehudit's exclusion.
However, Likud has denied conveying such messages.

"We are announcing the blocking of the Telegram application as part of efforts to strengthen digital security and protect users," the Public Security Directorate stated in a press release.
